## 2026-03-12 [Bug Fix] MCP rorca_list_specs and rorca_list_runs wrong response shape: Both tools assumed wrong API response shapes. rorca_list_specs treated response as a bare array but API returns { items: [...] }. rorca_list_runs destructured { runs } but API returns { items: [...] }. Fixed by normalizing: Array.isArray(data) ? data : (data.items ?? []) for list_specs, and payload.runs ?? payload.items ?? [] for list_runs. Also fixed specName field: API uses specName not title — display as s.specName ?? s.title ?? s.id.
> Rule: MCP rorca_list_specs and rorca_list_runs wrong response shape: Both tools assumed wrong API response shapes. rorca_list_specs treated response as a bare array but API returns { items: [...] }. rorca_list_runs destructured { runs } but API returns { items: [...] }. Fixed by normalizing: Array.isArray(data) ? data : (data.items ?? []) for list_specs, and payload.runs ?? payload.items ?? [] for list_runs. Also fixed specName field: API uses specName not title — display as s.specName ?? s.title ?? s.id.

## 2026-03-12 [Pattern] MCP tools vs prompts — tools are Claude-callable, prompts are user slash commands: MCP tools (server.registerTool) are called by Claude automatically during conversation. MCP prompts (server.registerPrompt) become user-invocable slash commands: /mcp__rorca__<name> [args]. Prompts use argsSchema (ZodRawShape, same as inputSchema for tools) and return { messages: [{ role: 'user', content: { type: 'text', text: '...' } }] }. All 24 Rorca tools now have corresponding prompt slash commands in backend/src/mcp/server.ts. Exceptions: edit_story, update_direction, create_workspace, team_members left as tools-only (complex multi-line inputs awkward as CLI args). generate_spec added as both tool AND prompt — takes quoted args: /mcp__rorca__generate_spec "slug" "brief".
> Rule: MCP tools vs prompts — tools are Claude-callable, prompts are user slash commands: MCP tools (server.registerTool) are called by Claude automatically during conversation. MCP prompts (server.registerPrompt) become user-invocable slash commands: /mcp__rorca__<name> [args]. Prompts use argsSchema (ZodRawShape, same as inputSchema for tools) and return { messages: [{ role: 'user', content: { type: 'text', text: '...' } }] }. All 24 Rorca tools now have corresponding prompt slash commands in backend/src/mcp/server.ts. Exceptions: edit_story, update_direction, create_workspace, team_members left as tools-only (complex multi-line inputs awkward as CLI args). generate_spec added as both tool AND prompt — takes quoted args: /mcp__rorca__generate_spec "slug" "brief".

## 2026-03-12 [Decision] When adding FK constraints to user-owned resources (e.g., uploaded_by), use ON DELETE SET NULL rather than CASCADE. CASCADE is only appropriate when the child record is conceptually owned by the parent.

## 2026-03-12 [Bug Fix] run-state.json and health-log.json must NOT be tracked by git: `.rorca/run-state.json` and `.rorca/memory/health-log.json` are in `.gitignore` but can end up tracked by git if committed before being ignored. When tracked, parallel worktree runs cause unresolved merge conflicts blocking all auto-merges. Fix: `git rm --cached .rorca/run-state.json .rorca/memory/health-log.json` + commit. Also add `.rorca-results.jsonl` to .gitignore — it's the WAL fallback file and causes add/add conflicts.
> Rule: run-state.json and health-log.json must NOT be tracked by git: `.rorca/run-state.json` and `.rorca/memory/health-log.json` are in `.gitignore` but can end up tracked by git if committed before being ignored. When tracked, parallel worktree runs cause unresolved merge conflicts blocking all auto-merges. Fix: `git rm --cached .rorca/run-state.json .rorca/memory/health-log.json` + commit. Also add `.rorca-results.jsonl` to .gitignore — it's the WAL fallback file and causes add/add conflicts.

## 2026-03-12 [Pattern] Worktree auto-merge conflict resolution pattern: When merging worktree branches back to main, these runtime files ALWAYS conflict — resolve them as follows: `progress.txt` → `git checkout --theirs`; `.rorca-results.jsonl` → `git checkout --theirs`; `.rorca/run-state.json` → `git rm --cached` (gitignored); `.rorca/memory/health-log.json` → `git rm --cached` (gitignored). Real code conflicts (pipeline.ts, specs.ts, mcp/server.ts) need manual resolution — always keep BOTH sides (HEAD routes + worktree routes). DB port is 5433 not 5432.
> Rule: Worktree auto-merge conflict resolution pattern: When merging worktree branches back to main, these runtime files ALWAYS conflict — resolve them as follows: `progress.txt` → `git checkout --theirs`; `.rorca-results.jsonl` → `git checkout --theirs`; `.rorca/run-state.json` → `git rm --cached` (gitignored); `.rorca/memory/health-log.json` → `git rm --cached` (gitignored). Real code conflicts (pipeline.ts, specs.ts, mcp/server.ts) need manual resolution — always keep BOTH sides (HEAD routes + worktree routes). DB port is 5433 not 5432.

## 2026-03-12 [Gotcha] Runs showing "failed" doesn't mean stories failed — check the log: When a run shows `status='failed'` in the DB, always check `forge/logs/run-N.log` first. Count `completed (exit 0)` entries. If stories completed but WAL calls returned HTTP 422, the code is in the worktree but results weren't posted. Recovery: check `git -C <worktree-path> log --oneline main..HEAD`, manually merge the worktree, then `UPDATE pipeline_runs SET status='done' WHERE id=N` via `psql -h localhost -p 5433 -U rorca -d rorca`.

## 2026-03-12 [Pattern] Express route handlers calling async database/utility functions must use `await`. Common offenders: `getVaultKey()`, `checkBudgetThresholds()`, `getCopilotToken()`, `getEffectiveUser()`, `resolveVaultCreds()`. If a helper is async, every call site needs `await` or type errors cascade.
> Rule: Express route handlers calling async database/utility functions must use `await`. Common offenders: `getVaultKey()`, `checkBudgetThresholds()`, `getCopilotToken()`, `getEffectiveUser()`, `resolveVaultCreds()`. If a helper is async, every call site needs `await` or type errors cascade.
> Source: QA-002

## 2026-03-12 [Gotcha] Express v5 types `req.params` values as `string | string[]`, not `string`. Cast to `string` when destructuring: `const { specId } = req.params as { specId: string }` or use a type assertion. Also, database query results from `queryOne<T>()` return `T | undefined` but functions expecting `T | null` need explicit `?? null` conversion.
> Rule: Express v5 types `req.params` values as `string | string[]`, not `string`. Cast to `string` when destructuring: `const { specId } = req.params as { specId: string }` or use a type assertion. Also, database query results from `queryOne<T>()` return `T | undefined` but functions expecting `T | null` need explicit `?? null` conversion.
> Source: QA-002

## 2026-03-12 [Bug Fix] PostgreSQL pg driver deserializes JSONB columns to JS objects automatically. When reading JSONB from wal_events or other tables, use defensive pattern: `typeof payload === 'string' ? JSON.parse(payload) : (payload ?? {})` instead of raw JSON.parse() to handle both string (legacy/raw SQL) and object (pg-deserialized) cases.
> Rule: PostgreSQL pg driver deserializes JSONB columns to JS objects automatically. When reading JSONB from wal_events or other tables, use defensive pattern: `typeof payload === 'string' ? JSON.parse(payload) : (payload ?? {})` instead of raw JSON.parse() to handle both string (legacy/raw SQL) and object (pg-deserialized) cases.
> Source: US-001

## 2026-03-12 [Gotcha] The wal_events table stores JSON in JSONB columns. When querying via pg Pool, the driver auto-deserializes JSONB to JS objects — the result is already an object, not a JSON string. Calling JSON.parse() on it throws SyntaxError. Always check type first or trust pg's deserialization.
> Rule: The wal_events table stores JSON in JSONB columns. When querying via pg Pool, the driver auto-deserializes JSONB to JS objects — the result is already an object, not a JSON string. Calling JSON.parse() on it throws SyntaxError. Always check type first or trust pg's deserialization.
> Source: US-001

## 2026-03-12 [Pattern] Postgres provisioning in `ensurePostgres()` should be idempotent at every step: check `.version` file to skip download, check data dir to skip initdb, use `isPortOpen()` to skip pg_ctl start, and use conditional creates (`createuser`/`createdb`) that swallow 'already exists' errors. This allows safe re-entry on any failure without manual cleanup.
> Rule: Postgres provisioning in `ensurePostgres()` should be idempotent at every step: check `.version` file to skip download, check data dir to skip initdb, use `isPortOpen()` to skip pg_ctl start, and use conditional creates (`createuser`/`createdb`) that swallow 'already exists' errors. This allows safe re-entry on any failure without manual cleanup.
> Source: US-005

## 2026-03-12 [Gotcha] Merging old SQLite-era branches with "take theirs" clobbers modern PostgreSQL files: NEVER merge old pre-postgres-migration branches (rorca-convention-agents, rorca-frontend-routing, and any branch with timestamp ~1772...) using "git checkout --theirs" on code conflicts. These branches were built on SQLite and will revert db/index.ts to the SQLite version, revert App.tsx/Sidebar.tsx/routes.tsx to the old multi-panel UI, and truncate server.ts. Always restore from a known-good modern commit (e.g. git show <pre-merge-sha>:path/to/file) after any such merge.
> Rule: Merging old SQLite-era branches with "take theirs" clobbers modern PostgreSQL files: NEVER merge old pre-postgres-migration branches (rorca-convention-agents, rorca-frontend-routing, and any branch with timestamp ~1772...) using "git checkout --theirs" on code conflicts. These branches were built on SQLite and will revert db/index.ts to the SQLite version, revert App.tsx/Sidebar.tsx/routes.tsx to the old multi-panel UI, and truncate server.ts. Always restore from a known-good modern commit (e.g. git show <pre-merge-sha>:path/to/file) after any such merge.

## 2026-03-12 [Bug Fix] mod+shift+r hotkey hijacked browser hard refresh (Cmd+Shift+R): Do not bind mod+shift+r (Cmd+Shift+R) as a hotkey in the app — it is the browser's hard refresh shortcut on macOS. The hotkey was bound to navigate('/runs'), so every hard refresh silently redirected the user to the Runs page instead of refreshing. Fixed by removing the binding from the hotkeys array in App.tsx.
> Rule: mod+shift+r hotkey hijacked browser hard refresh (Cmd+Shift+R): Do not bind mod+shift+r (Cmd+Shift+R) as a hotkey in the app — it is the browser's hard refresh shortcut on macOS. The hotkey was bound to navigate('/runs'), so every hard refresh silently redirected the user to the Runs page instead of refreshing. Fixed by removing the binding from the hotkeys array in App.tsx.

## 2026-03-12 [Decision] rorca-ensure-postgres completed — zero-prereq Postgres provisioning in bin/rorca.ts: bin/rorca.ts now includes a full ensurePostgres() function. On first run, it downloads Postgres 16 binaries from zonkyio/embedded-postgres-binaries, extracts, runs initdb, starts pg_ctl on port 5433, creates rorca user and database. No Docker required. DATABASE_URL env var bypasses this entirely (preserves Docker workflow). --no-postgres flag also skips it. Postgres is stopped on SIGINT/SIGTERM via stopManagedPostgres().
> Rule: rorca-ensure-postgres completed — zero-prereq Postgres provisioning in bin/rorca.ts: bin/rorca.ts now includes a full ensurePostgres() function. On first run, it downloads Postgres 16 binaries from zonkyio/embedded-postgres-binaries, extracts, runs initdb, starts pg_ctl on port 5433, creates rorca user and database. No Docker required. DATABASE_URL env var bypasses this entirely (preserves Docker workflow). --no-postgres flag also skips it. Postgres is stopped on SIGINT/SIGTERM via stopManagedPostgres().

## 2026-03-12 [Bug Fix] tsx watch restarts backend during parallel runs → resilient-post retries exhaust: When a fast worktree run auto-merges into main, tsx watch detects the file changes and restarts the backend (5-10s TypeScript recompile). If resilient-post.ts retry window is shorter than the restart time, execution engine can't report story results and the run shows as failed. Fix: raise POST_MAX_RETRIES to 10 and POST_RETRY_DELAY_MS to 3000 (30s coverage) in backend/src/lib/resilient-post.ts.
> Rule: tsx watch restarts backend during parallel runs → resilient-post retries exhaust: When a fast worktree run auto-merges into main, tsx watch detects the file changes and restarts the backend (5-10s TypeScript recompile). If resilient-post.ts retry window is shorter than the restart time, execution engine can't report story results and the run shows as failed. Fix: raise POST_MAX_RETRIES to 10 and POST_RETRY_DELAY_MS to 3000 (30s coverage) in backend/src/lib/resilient-post.ts.

## 2026-03-13 [Gotcha] Parallel feature branches cause duplicate migration numbers: Migration runner keys on the numeric version extracted from the filename (e.g. 069 from 069_foo.sql). If two branches independently create a migration with the same number, the runner applies the first alphabetically and silently skips the second. Always check the highest migration number in schema_migrations before creating a new migration file. Fix: rename the conflicting file to the next available number and INSERT the new version into schema_migrations manually.

Always check the highest migration number in schema_migrations before creating a new migration file. Fix: rename the conflicting file to the next available number and INSERT the new version into schema_migrations manually.

Any direct pgboss.job queries must use started_on, completed_on, expire_in (not expirein), etc.

## 2026-03-13 [Bug Fix] Kill button silent fail — activeProcesses map empty after worker restart: The cancel route sends a pipeline:cancel pg-boss job to the worker, which looks up activeProcesses.get(runId). If the worker was restarted since the run started, activeProcesses is empty and no SIGTERM is sent — the HTTP call returns 200 but the process is never killed. WR-010 added a dead-PID fallback: when activeProcesses misses, fall back to the pid stored in pipeline_runs and kill directly. Now live in main.

## 2026-03-13 [Gotcha] 150+ unmerged feat/ branches accumulate — audit regularly: Worktree spec runs create feat/ branches that never auto-merge. After several months of development, 150+ branches can accumulate. Most are stale (superseded by later runs of the same spec). When auditing: (1) check remote feat/ branches with commits not in main using `git branch -r | grep feat/ | while read b; do count=$(git log --oneline main.."$b" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); if [ "$count" -gt "0" ]; then echo "$count | $b"; fi; done`, (2) skip old pg-boss/scaffolding branches — their work is superseded by WR spec, (3) merge the most recent run of each spec (highest timestamp suffix = most complete), (4) skip convention-agents branches (old stubs, superseded by future spec).

## 2026-03-13 [Bug Fix] completedon → completed_on in pgboss.job UPDATE queries: pg-boss internal schema uses snake_case with underscores for ALL column names: started_on, completed_on, completed_after, expire_in. NOT startedon, completedon, etc. Affected reconcileState (Case B) and recoverStaleJobs — both silently failed on every 30s tick, leaving stale active pgboss.job rows that block new runs from being picked up. Fixed 2026-03-13 in worker.ts. When writing any direct pgboss.job or pgboss.archive queries, always use underscored column names.

Fixed 2026-03-13 in worker.ts. When writing any direct pgboss.job or pgboss.archive queries, always use underscored column names.

## 2026-03-13 [Gotcha] Old execution-engine processes from test runs survive indefinitely: Execution-engine subprocesses from old load test runs (WR-019, PG-020) and integration tests in temp paths can survive machine restarts and run for days, consuming CPU/memory. Check with: `ps aux | grep execution-engine | grep -v grep`. Kill PIDs associated with temp paths (/var/folders, /tmp) or old worktree paths. WR-007 graceful shutdown only helps for clean worker exits — kill -9 or machine crash still orphans children. Safe to kill any execution-engine with a temp path or a worktree path that no longer exists.

## 2026-03-13 [Decision] MCP-native generation: API as context+persistence layer, LLM work in caller's session: Rorca's API should split LLM-heavy operations (spec generation, enrichment) into two phases: (1) context-fetch — API returns the synthesized direction stack, memory, schema, skills as a raw bundle with no LLM call; (2) save — API persists the result the caller's LLM already generated. The LLM reasoning happens IN the caller's MCP session (Claude Code, OpenCode CLI, Codex CLI), not in a server-spawned subprocess. This means: rorca_get_generation_context returns the context bundle, the calling LLM generates the spec JSON in-session using cached/warm context, then rorca_save_spec persists it. The existing server-side generation path (spawning claude --print) is kept as a fallback for browser UI users who have no MCP session. This is the correct long-term architecture for rorca_forge_and_run too — it should orchestrate tool calls that the caller's session handles, not block on a subprocess.
> Rule: MCP-native generation: API as context+persistence layer, LLM work in caller's session: Rorca's API should split LLM-heavy operations (spec generation, enrichment) into two phases: (1) context-fetch — API returns the synthesized direction stack, memory, schema, skills as a raw bundle with no LLM call; (2) save — API persists the result the caller's LLM already generated. The LLM reasoning happens IN the caller's MCP session (Claude Code, OpenCode CLI, Codex CLI), not in a server-spawned subprocess. This means: rorca_get_generation_context returns the context bundle, the calling LLM generates the spec JSON in-session using cached/warm context, then rorca_save_spec persists it. The existing server-side generation path (spawning claude --print) is kept as a fallback for browser UI users who have no MCP session. This is the correct long-term architecture for rorca_forge_and_run too — it should orchestrate tool calls that the caller's session handles, not block on a subprocess.

Alternatives considered: Current approach: POST /api/specs/generate always spawns a fresh claude --print subprocess with cold context (~3000 token overhead per call, no caching). This wastes tokens and is slower. Alternative considered: keeping server-side generation for all paths — rejected because it means every spec generation spins up a new Claude process even when the user is already in a warm Claude/OpenCode/Codex session with full context cached. Alternative: HTTP transport MCP with auto-detection of caller type — the API could detect whether the request comes from an MCP client vs browser and return context-only vs run the subprocess. This is the cleanest path and aligns with the HTTP transport MCP roadmap already in CLAUDE.md.

## 2026-03-13 [Architecture] All three CLI coding assistants support MCP — Rorca tools work from any of them: Claude Code, OpenCode CLI, and Codex CLI all support MCP servers. A user working in any of these three can call Rorca MCP tools (rorca_generate_spec, rorca_trigger_run, etc.) from their active session. The only path that does NOT support MCP is the browser UI. This means the MCP-native generation architecture benefits all CLI users regardless of which assistant they use: Claude Code (Claude model), OpenCode CLI (any provider — GPT-4o, Gemini, etc.), Codex CLI (ChatGPT model). Architecture principle: Rorca API = context + persistence. LLM reasoning = caller's session. Browser UI = server-side subprocess fallback only.
> Rule: All three CLI coding assistants support MCP — Rorca tools work from any of them: Claude Code, OpenCode CLI, and Codex CLI all support MCP servers. A user working in any of these three can call Rorca MCP tools (rorca_generate_spec, rorca_trigger_run, etc.) from their active session. The only path that does NOT support MCP is the browser UI. This means the MCP-native generation architecture benefits all CLI users regardless of which assistant they use: Claude Code (Claude model), OpenCode CLI (any provider — GPT-4o, Gemini, etc.), Codex CLI (ChatGPT model). Architecture principle: Rorca API = context + persistence. LLM reasoning = caller's session. Browser UI = server-side subprocess fallback only.

## 2026-03-14 [Bug Fix] AGE search_path pool poisoning — intermittent "Workspace not found" 404s: Any code that calls setupAgeSession() (LOAD 'age' + SET search_path = ag_catalog) MUST restore the search_path before releasing the pool connection: `await client.query('SET search_path = rorca, public')` in the finally block before `client.release()`. Without this, the pool connection retains ag_catalog as the first schema, causing subsequent queries to hit ag_catalog.workspaces (empty) instead of rorca.workspaces (real data) — producing intermittent "Workspace not found" 404s across all routes.
> Rule: AGE search_path pool poisoning — intermittent "Workspace not found" 404s: Any code that calls setupAgeSession() (LOAD 'age' + SET search_path = ag_catalog) MUST restore the search_path before releasing the pool connection: `await client.query('SET search_path = rorca, public')` in the finally block before `client.release()`. Without this, the pool connection retains ag_catalog as the first schema, causing subsequent queries to hit ag_catalog.workspaces (empty) instead of rorca.workspaces (real data) — producing intermittent "Workspace not found" 404s across all routes.

## 2026-03-14 [Gotcha] PostgreSQL BIGINT returned as strings by pg driver — must coerce with Number(): The node-pg driver returns BIGINT column values as JavaScript strings, not numbers. When comparing BIGINT values with parseInt() results (e.g. in Set.has() lookups), always coerce with Number(r.version) when building the Set. Without this, Set.has(1) won't match "1" and the migration runner would try to re-apply every migration on every startup.

When comparing BIGINT values with parseInt() results (e.g. in Set.has() lookups), always coerce with Number(r.version) when building the Set. Without this, Set.has(1) won't match "1" and the migration runner would try to re-apply every migration on every startup.

## 2026-03-14 [Decision] Hybrid migration strategy — keep sequential 001-079, timestamps going forward: Do NOT rename existing sequential migrations (001-079) to timestamp format. The hybrid approach is intentional: existing migrations keep their numbers, new migrations use YYYYMMDDHHMMSS. The runner's numeric sort naturally orders timestamps after sequential numbers (79 < 20260314150000). Renaming 79+ existing files and updating schema_migrations records is high-risk with no benefit — the old migrations are already applied and immutable.

## 2026-03-15 [Bug Fix] pipeline:cron backlog floods worker on restart — starves pipeline:run jobs: When the worker is down, the scheduler (running in the API server) keeps queuing pipeline:cron meta-tick jobs — one per minute. On worker restart, hundreds of cron ticks flood the pipeline:cron queue (batchSize:10, fires every 2s). This saturates the worker's polling loop and can cause pipeline:run jobs to be picked up silently but die mid-process, ending up as stale 'active' jobs that recoverStaleJobs() then marks failed. Any pipeline:run job that was queued while the worker was down may need to be re-triggered after the worker restarts.

Any code that checks for 'stuck' runs must account for this: queued runs without pg-boss jobs are normal, not orphaned.

## 2026-03-16 [Bug Fix] payload::text LIKE queries cause pool exhaustion under wave parallelism: Never use `payload::text LIKE '%"run_id":N%'` on wal_events. Always use `(payload->>'run_id')::int = $N` — JSONB accessor is 10x faster and doesn't cause full table scans. Critical under wave parallelism (18+ concurrent SSE connections each polling WAL).
> Rule: payload::text LIKE queries cause pool exhaustion under wave parallelism: Never use `payload::text LIKE '%"run_id":N%'` on wal_events. Always use `(payload->>'run_id')::int = $N` — JSONB accessor is 10x faster and doesn't cause full table scans. Critical under wave parallelism (18+ concurrent SSE connections each polling WAL).

Fix: change to `{ teamSize: currentMaxConcurrent, batchSize: currentMaxConcurrent }`. Same bug on pipeline:retry at line 2149. Until fixed, only 1 pipeline run executes at a time regardless of max_concurrent_runs setting.

Deferred to a separate spec. Short-term: concurrent Running indicators in story list (US-005, done) make parallelism visible without splitting the terminal.

Alternatives considered: ANSI boundary markers in stream: fragile to parse, breaks if output contains similar sequences. Separate runId per story: requires major schema refactor across all child tables. story_id column on run_output_chunks: correct fix, needs migration + execution-engine changes to tag chunks by story on write.

## 2026-03-16 [Decision] pipeline_runs.id widened to BIGINT, sequence restarted at 20260316000000: Applied migration 20260316141659_pipeline_runs_seq_restart.sql on 2026-03-16. pipeline_runs.id and all child run_id columns (story_results, run_output_chunks, token_usage, memory_proposals) widened from INTEGER to BIGINT. pipeline_runs_id_seq widened AS BIGINT and restarted at 20260316000000. Old runs #1–#133 keep sequential IDs. New runs get timestamp-ish IDs (20260316000001, 20260316000002, ...). ## 2026-03-16 [Bug Fix] pg-boss v10 has no teamSize — concurrent runs need Promise.allSettled in handler: pg-boss v10 WorkOptions only has batchSize (how many jobs fetched per poll) — there is no teamSize or concurrency option. The handler receives Job[] and the original code used `for (const job of jobs)` which processed them sequentially. Fix: wrap handler body in `await Promise.allSettled(jobs.map(async (job) => { ... }))` so all fetched jobs spawn child processes concurrently. Applied to both handlePipelineRun and handlePipelineRetry in worker.ts.

Applied to both handlePipelineRun and handlePipelineRetry in worker.ts.

## 2026-03-16 [Bug Fix] BIGINT run IDs break ::int casts in WAL queries — must use ::bigint: After widening pipeline_runs.id to BIGINT and restarting the sequence at 20260316000000, all SQL queries that extract run_id from JSON payloads via (payload->>'run_id')::int will overflow INT4 (max 2147483647). Changed 13 occurrences in pipeline.ts and 3 in worker.ts from ::int to ::bigint. This affects per-story SSE endpoint, WAL event lookups, story output queries, and pg-boss job lookups.

## 2026-03-16 [Bug Fix] pg driver returns BIGINT as string — Zod schemas need z.coerce.number(): PostgreSQL's pg driver returns BIGINT columns as JavaScript strings (not numbers) because JS Number can't represent all BIGINT values. After the pipeline_runs.id BIGINT migration, RETURNING id returns "20260316000003" (string). The Zod schema PipelineRunJobPayload used z.number().int().positive() which rejected strings. Fix: changed all runId validators to z.coerce.number().int().positive() in pg-boss-schemas.ts. This coerces string→number safely since our IDs (~2*10^13) are well within Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (~9*10^15).

This coerces string→number safely since our IDs (~2*10^13) are well within Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (~9*10^15).

## 2026-03-16 [Decision] Use Promise.allSettled for pg-boss concurrent job handling instead of teamSize: pg-boss v10 removed the teamSize option that controlled concurrent handler invocations. The handler receives Job[] (batch) and must parallelize internally. We chose Promise.allSettled(jobs.map(...)) over Promise.all because allSettled allows individual job failures without failing the entire batch — critical since pipeline runs can take 45+ minutes and one failure shouldn't abort sibling runs.
> Rule: Use Promise.allSettled for pg-boss concurrent job handling instead of teamSize: pg-boss v10 removed the teamSize option that controlled concurrent handler invocations. The handler receives Job[] (batch) and must parallelize internally. We chose Promise.allSettled(jobs.map(...)) over Promise.all because allSettled allows individual job failures without failing the entire batch — critical since pipeline runs can take 45+ minutes and one failure shouldn't abort sibling runs.

Alternatives considered: 1) Promise.all — rejected because one job throwing would fail the entire batch and abort sibling runs. 2) Upgrade to pg-boss v11+ which may have teamConcurrency — rejected because major version upgrade carries risk and our fix is simple. 3) Use batchSize:1 and rely on polling interval — rejected because it would still be sequential (one job per poll cycle).

This caused config.worktreePath to always be null, silently preventing auto-merge from ever firing. Fixed by adding the three pushes after the startFromStoryId block (worker.ts ~line 722).

## 2026-03-16 [Architecture] Worktree lifecycle design — one worktree per spec, not per run: Branch name is feat/<slug> (no timestamp) — deterministic per spec. On trigger: reuse existing worktree dir if it exists (skip git worktree add). On all stories pass: auto-merge to main + git worktree remove --force. On partial/full fail: leave worktree intact for retry. Retry reuses the same directory and skips already-passing stories. Merge gate: only merges to main when every non-excluded story has passed.
> Rule: Worktree lifecycle design — one worktree per spec, not per run: Branch name is feat/<slug> (no timestamp) — deterministic per spec. On trigger: reuse existing worktree dir if it exists (skip git worktree add). On all stories pass: auto-merge to main + git worktree remove --force. ## 2026-03-17 [Bug Fix] Orphan sweep kills all runs — worker_id never set on pipeline_runs: Both handlePipelineRun and handlePipelineRetry must include `worker_id = $2` in the UPDATE pipeline_runs SET status = 'running' statement. Without it, pr.worker_id IS NULL and the orphan sweep matches every active run, killing them after ~5 minutes.

## 2026-03-17 [Gotcha] BIGINT from pg driver breaks Map.has() — activeProcesses lookup silently fails: The `pg` driver returns PostgreSQL BIGINT columns as JavaScript strings, not numbers. `activeProcesses` is `Map<number, ChildProcess>`, so `activeProcesses.has("20260316000008")` always returns false even if the key `20260316000008` (number) exists. Always coerce with `Number(run.id)` when using pg-returned IDs as Map keys.
> Rule: BIGINT from pg driver breaks Map.has() — activeProcesses lookup silently fails: The `pg` driver returns PostgreSQL BIGINT columns as JavaScript strings, not numbers. `activeProcesses` is `Map<number, ChildProcess>`, so `activeProcesses.has("20260316000008")` always returns false even if the key `20260316000008` (number) exists. Always coerce with `Number(run.id)` when using pg-returned IDs as Map keys.

The local catch handler returns a 500. Instead use `res.status(404).json({ error: 'Run not in DLQ' }); return;` directly.

## 2026-03-17 [Bug Fix] MultiPaneTerminal wave grouping broken — wave_index missing from story_started WAL events: executeStory() must accept a `waveIndex?: number` parameter and include it in the story_started WAL event payload as `wave_index`. ## 2026-03-17 [Bug Fix] WAL SSE delay: seed usePipelineSSE from REST before live stream: usePipelineSSE now fetches GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/wal-events on runId change to immediately seed historical events. Without this, /api/pipeline/stream starts replaying from lastSeenId=0 at LIMIT 50/tick — causing a 5+ minute delay before story_started events for the current run arrive. Live SSE events are deduplicated against the seed by event id.

## 2026-03-17 [Bug Fix] Semantic log parser: tool_use is inside assistant.message.content[], not top-level: Claude stream-json (--output-format stream-json) NEVER emits standalone {"type":"tool_use",...} events. Tool calls are embedded inside the assistant event at message.content[] as {type:"tool_use", name, input} blocks. The parser must iterate assistant.message.content[] — not look for top-level type=tool_use. parseLine() and all parse functions return SemanticStep[] (not SemanticStep|null).

## 2026-03-17 [Bug Fix] Single-story wave merge fails on .rorca/run-state.json conflict — outer+inner worktree both write it: When a run uses an outer worktree (auto-merge) + inner wave worktrees, `mergeStoryWorktree` pre-commits dirty files in the outer worktree (including `.rorca/run-state.json`), creating a divergence from the inner story worktree which also wrote `run-state.json`. Git cannot auto-merge JSON, so `git merge --no-ff` fails. US-001 (or any single-story wave) is added to `failedIds`, cascade-blocking all downstream stories. Fixed by auto-resolving conflicts on runtime-only files (`--ours`) before falling through to hard failure.
> Rule: Single-story wave merge fails on .rorca/run-state.json conflict — outer+inner worktree both write it: When a run uses an outer worktree (auto-merge) + inner wave worktrees, `mergeStoryWorktree` pre-commits dirty files in the outer worktree (including `.rorca/run-state.json`), creating a divergence from the inner story worktree which also wrote `run-state.json`. Git cannot auto-merge JSON, so `git merge --no-ff` fails. US-001 (or any single-story wave) is added to `failedIds`, cascade-blocking all downstream stories. Fixed by auto-resolving conflicts on runtime-only files (`--ours`) before falling through to hard failure.

## 2026-03-17 [Gotcha] execSync merge errors: log err.stderr not err.message — "Command failed" is useless: When `execSync` throws on a failed git command, `err.message` only contains "Command failed: git merge ..." — the actual git error (conflict details, stderr output) is in `err.stderr` as a Buffer. Always log `err.stderr?.toString().trim()` first, fall back to `err.message`. Cast as `Error & { stderr?: Buffer }` for TypeScript.
> Rule: execSync merge errors: log err.stderr not err.message — "Command failed" is useless: When `execSync` throws on a failed git command, `err.message` only contains "Command failed: git merge ..." — the actual git error (conflict details, stderr output) is in `err.stderr` as a Buffer. Always log `err.stderr?.toString().trim()` first, fall back to `err.message`. Cast as `Error & { stderr?: Buffer }` for TypeScript.

## 2026-03-17 [Pattern] Diagnose run failures: query run_output_chunks + grep msg field from JSON logs: To see the full execution log for any run (including errors scrolled off in the terminal), query: `psql postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca -t -c "SELECT encode(chunk,'escape') FROM run_output_chunks WHERE run_id = <id> ORDER BY sequence" | grep -o '"msg":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"msg":"//;s/"$//'`. The column is `chunk` (bytea), not `data`. Port is 5433, database is `rorca`.
> Rule: Diagnose run failures: query run_output_chunks + grep msg field from JSON logs: To see the full execution log for any run (including errors scrolled off in the terminal), query: `psql postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca -t -c "SELECT encode(chunk,'escape') FROM run_output_chunks WHERE run_id = <id> ORDER BY sequence" | grep -o '"msg":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"msg":"//;s/"$//'`. The column is `chunk` (bytea), not `data`. Port is 5433, database is `rorca`.

## 2026-03-17 [Bug Fix] SSE live stream 5-minute delay — root cause and fix: GET /api/pipeline/stream started lastSeenId=0 every connection, replaying ALL historical WAL events at LIMIT 50/tick. With 5000+ events this caused 5+ minute delay before live events appeared. Fix: initialize lastSeenId to MAX(id) FROM wal_events on connection open. Historical events served instantly by new REST endpoint GET /runs/:runId/wal-events. Combined: usePipelineSSE seeds history from REST (immediate), SSE stream delivers only new events (within 3s).
> Rule: SSE live stream 5-minute delay — root cause and fix: GET /api/pipeline/stream started lastSeenId=0 every connection, replaying ALL historical WAL events at LIMIT 50/tick. With 5000+ events this caused 5+ minute delay before live events appeared. Fix: initialize lastSeenId to MAX(id) FROM wal_events on connection open. Historical events served instantly by new REST endpoint GET /runs/:runId/wal-events. Combined: usePipelineSSE seeds history from REST (immediate), SSE stream delivers only new events (within 3s).

## 2026-03-17 [Bug Fix] Merge failure leaves passes:true — idempotency gap causes next run to skip story with no code: When a sub-worktree merge fails, markStoryPassed() had already written passes:true to the spec JSON. The failure path added the story to failedIds and emitted story_failed WAL event, but never reverted passes:true. Next run sees passes:true, skips the story, but the code is not in the parent branch. Fix: call markStoryMergeFailed() in both merge failure paths (single-story wave at line ~3154, multi-story wave failures at line ~3219). markStoryMergeFailed() sets passes:false, clears skipped, adds a note.
> Rule: Merge failure leaves passes:true — idempotency gap causes next run to skip story with no code: When a sub-worktree merge fails, markStoryPassed() had already written passes:true to the spec JSON. The failure path added the story to failedIds and emitted story_failed WAL event, but never reverted passes:true. Next run sees passes:true, skips the story, but the code is not in the parent branch. Fix: call markStoryMergeFailed() in both merge failure paths (single-story wave at line ~3154, multi-story wave failures at line ~3219). markStoryMergeFailed() sets passes:false, clears skipped, adds a note.

## 2026-03-17 [Bug Fix] Worker premature auto-merge — status=done without all stories passing triggered merge: worker.ts was merging the parent worktree into main when status==='done' regardless of whether all spec stories passed. A run can be 'done' with 0 stories executed (immediate exit). Fix: before calling autoMergeAfterRun, read the spec JSON and verify every story has passes===true or excluded===true. Only merge if allSpecStoriesPassed is true.

## 2026-03-17 [Gotcha] tsx module cache causes routes to return 404 after file edits — fresh restart required: After adding a new route to pipeline.ts, the route returned 404 despite being in the source and other routes in the same file working. tsx watch auto-restarts do not always invalidate the compiled module cache. `touch` on the file does not fix it. A full kill+restart (lsof -ti:3030 | xargs kill -9, then npm run dev) forces tsx to recompile from scratch and register all routes. Never diagnose a 404 for a route that exists in source without first doing a full restart.

Never diagnose a 404 for a route that exists in source without first doing a full restart.

## 2026-03-17 [Architecture] WAL event streaming architecture — two-track design for instant history + live events: Two endpoints work together: (1) REST GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/wal-events returns all past WAL events for a run instantly via direct DB query. (2) SSE GET /api/pipeline/stream delivers live events only (starts at MAX WAL id). usePipelineSSE.ts: on runId change, immediately seeds from REST then deduplicates live SSE events by id. useWalSSE singleton: single EventSource shared across all components (avoids Chrome 6-connection limit). Never use SSE alone for historical data — always pair with REST seed.

Never use SSE alone for historical data — always pair with REST seed.

## 2026-03-17 [Gotcha] Never kill backend while a run is active — execution engine WAL writes will fail: The execution engine (child of worker, not of server) sends WAL events via fetch to http://localhost:3030/api/wal. If the server is killed mid-run, those WAL writes fail silently and events are lost. The run continues but story progress disappears from the UI. The run stays stuck as status=running in the DB with no finished_at. Always confirm no active runs (GET /api/pipeline/worker/health activeJobs=[]) before killing the backend.

## 2026-03-17 [Gotcha] Worker process must be manually restarted after worker.ts changes: Plain `tsx` (not `tsx watch`) is used for the worker — it does NOT hot-reload on file changes. Any change to `backend/src/worker.ts` requires killing the worker process and restarting it. The backend (Express) auto-restarts via tsx watch, but the worker is completely separate. Always verify worker PID start time vs file modification time before assuming a fix is live.

The merge-base approach checks the actual commit SHA from git worktree list against main's ancestry chain.

## 2026-03-18 [Gotcha] Worktree auto-merge fails silently when concurrent specs touch overlapping files: When two specs run concurrently in separate worktrees and edit the same files, the auto-merge of the second worktree fails with real merge conflicts. The run is left stuck as 'running' and implementation files remain stranded in the feature branch. Recovery requires: (1) manual git merge with conflict resolution, (2) restoring dropped files via `git show <sha>:path > file`, (3) manually marking the run as failed in the DB.

Recovery requires: (1) manual git merge with conflict resolution, (2) restoring dropped files via `git show <sha>:path > file`, (3) manually marking the run as failed in the DB.

## 2026-03-18 [Architecture] Memory consolidation: DB is source of truth, MEMORY.md is optional projection: DB memories table is the single source of truth. MEMORY.md is a generated read-only projection rebuilt pre/post run — never written by agents directly. rorca_recall and rorca_get_memories (with fetchAll:true) both read from DB. rorca_dump is deprecated. MEMORY.md is only worth keeping if the workspace is used outside Rorca (Cursor, Copilot, raw Claude Code) — it is redundant in a Rorca-only workflow.

## 2026-03-18 [Architecture] Simultaneous spec runs require autoWorktree: Running multiple specs simultaneously (sequential OR wave-parallel) requires autoWorktree: true on each run. Without a worktree, the conflict detection in pipeline.ts blocks any new run if another is already running in the same workspace. With autoWorktree, up to run_now_max_concurrent (default 3) runs can coexist, each in an isolated git worktree branch.

## 2026-03-18 [Bug Fix] StoryLogFollower never fires from live WAL subscription — JSONB payload parsed as object not string: StoryLogFollower.onStoryStarted and onStoryFinished called JSON.parse(event.payload) but wal_events.payload is JSONB — pg returns it as a JS object, not a string. JSON.parse on an object calls .toString() → "[object Object]" → SyntaxError → catch returns silently. Fix: check typeof event.payload === 'string' before parsing, otherwise use the object directly. recover() was unaffected because it casts payload::text in SQL.
> Rule: StoryLogFollower never fires from live WAL subscription — JSONB payload parsed as object not string: StoryLogFollower.onStoryStarted and onStoryFinished called JSON.parse(event.payload) but wal_events.payload is JSONB — pg returns it as a JS object, not a string. JSON.parse on an object calls .toString() → "[object Object]" → SyntaxError → catch returns silently. Fix: check typeof event.payload === 'string' before parsing, otherwise use the object directly. recover() was unaffected because it casts payload::text in SQL.

## 2026-03-19 [Bug Fix] tsx ENOENT when worker spawns execution engine: Worker spawns execution-engine via `path.join(__dirname, '..', 'node_modules', '.bin', 'tsx')` — fails with ENOENT when tsx not in backend/node_modules. Root cause: root postinstall runs `cd backend && npm install --production --ignore-scripts` which skips devDependencies (tsx is a devDep). Fix: added `findTsxBin()` helper in worker.ts — tries local path first, falls back to `which tsx`. Also run `cd backend && npm install` to install all deps. Symptom: run fails in <100ms with "spawn ... tsx ENOENT".

## 2026-03-19 [Bug Fix] Silent terminal — execution-engine block.text missing trailing newline: execution-engine.ts wrote `process.stdout.write(block.text)` without a trailing `\n`. RunTerminal.tsx uses a line-buffer pattern: `parts.pop()` keeps any "incomplete last line" (one without `\n`) in `lineBufferRef` indefinitely — it never reaches `displayLines` and is never rendered. Fix: `process.stdout.write(block.text.endsWith('\n') ? block.text : block.text + '\n')` at the point where claude stream-json assistant blocks are emitted to stdout (execution-engine.ts ~line 744). Non-JSON fallback already had `+ '\n'` and worked correctly.

Non-JSON fallback already had `+ '\n'` and worked correctly.

## 2026-03-19 [Gotcha] run_output_chunks schema: column is "chunk" not "data", DB port is 5433: run_output_chunks table columns: `(id, run_id, chunk BYTEA, sequence INT, created_at)`. Column is `chunk`, NOT `data`. Also: DATABASE_URL uses port 5433 not default 5432 — `postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca`. pg-boss table uses `created_on` not `createdon`. Always read backend/.env before writing raw SQL queries.

## 2026-03-19 [Decision] Task-Monitor pattern: pg-boss jobs complete immediately, reconcileState is the watchdog: pg-boss jobs must NOT stay active for the lifetime of an execution engine subprocess. The job spawns the engine and returns immediately (fire-and-forget). Engine liveness is monitored via IPC heartbeats (every 60s) written to pipeline_runs.last_heartbeat. reconcileState() runs every 60s as the watchdog: if last_heartbeat > 2 min stale AND PID is dead → mark run failed. expireInSeconds should be 300s (not hours).

## 2026-03-19 [Decision] DB-based per-workspace concurrency lock replaces in-memory activeTriggeredVia: Concurrency uses SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pipeline_runs WHERE workspace_id=$1 AND status='running' before spawning. The old in-memory activeTriggeredVia map was removed. Worktree runs bypass the lock. DB is the single source of truth, supports horizontal scaling.
> Rule: DB-based per-workspace concurrency lock replaces in-memory activeTriggeredVia: Concurrency uses SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pipeline_runs WHERE workspace_id=$1 AND status='running' before spawning. ## 2026-03-19 [Gotcha] Never have workers kill each other — fix process management instead: Worker singleton guard must NEVER SIGTERM/SIGKILL other worker PIDs. In distributed environments, workers would assassinate each other. The zombie child problem is a process management issue — use --kill-others on concurrently or proper supervisor signal propagation.

## 2026-03-20 [Bug Fix] GitHub OAuth 503 — tsx/esbuild module-level env var capture: Module-level constants like `const GITHUB_CLIENT_ID = process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID || ''` capture empty strings because tsx/esbuild hoists all require() calls before dotenv.config() runs. Fix: use lazy getter functions that call process.env at request time: `function githubClientId() { return process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID || ''; }`
> Rule: GitHub OAuth 503 — tsx/esbuild module-level env var capture: Module-level constants like `const GITHUB_CLIENT_ID = process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID || ''` capture empty strings because tsx/esbuild hoists all require() calls before dotenv.config() runs. Fix: use lazy getter functions that call process.env at request time: `function githubClientId() { return process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID || ''; }`

## 2026-03-20 [Bug Fix] Migration runner poisoning pool search_path (pg-index.ts): pg-index.ts runPgMigrations() sets `SET search_path TO public` but never restores it before releasing the pool connection. This poisons the reused connection — subsequent code (e.g. seedWorkerSettings) runs with search_path=public and cannot see rorca.* tables. Fix: in the `finally` block, run `SET search_path TO rorca, public` before client.release(). Same class of bug as AGE pool poisoning.

Fix: in the `finally` block, run `SET search_path TO rorca, public` before client.release(). Same class of bug as AGE pool poisoning.

## 2026-03-20 [Bug Fix] Two schema_migrations tables — public vs rorca schema split: There are TWO schema_migrations tables: `public.schema_migrations` (used by migration runner after search_path fix) and `rorca.schema_migrations` (used before the fix). Migrations applied before the fix are only in `rorca.schema_migrations`. On fresh server starts, the runner tries to re-run them and fails on non-idempotent ones (e.g. 057). Fix applied 2026-03-20: upgraded public.schema_migrations.version to BIGINT and copied all missing rows from rorca.schema_migrations. Also: public.schema_migrations was INTEGER not BIGINT — had to ALTER COLUMN before copying timestamp versions (20260316+).

Migrations applied before the fix are only in `rorca.schema_migrations`. On fresh server starts, the runner tries to re-run them and fails on non-idempotent ones (e.g. 057). Also: public.schema_migrations was INTEGER not BIGINT — had to ALTER COLUMN before copying timestamp versions (20260316+).

## 2026-03-20 [Bug Fix] GitHub account endpoint always returning connected:false (LIMIT 1 on users): workspace-github.ts GET /account used `SELECT id FROM users LIMIT 1` to find the "current user", which always returns admin@rorca.local (created first by migration seed). The GitHub-authenticated user (dteravan@gmail.com) is a different row and has the github_connections entry. Fix: query github_connections directly without going through users first: `SELECT gc.*, u.avatar_url FROM github_connections gc JOIN users u ON gc.user_id = u.id ORDER BY gc.created_at DESC LIMIT 1`

## 2026-03-20 [Pattern] sessionStorage return URL for OAuth flows: Before triggering any full-page OAuth redirect, store the return destination in sessionStorage: `sessionStorage.setItem('github_oauth_return', '/settings/github')`. In the callback page, read it: `const returnTo = sessionStorage.getItem('github_oauth_return') || '/'; sessionStorage.removeItem('github_oauth_return'); navigate(returnTo, { replace: true })`. Without this, OAuth callbacks always land on '/' which React Router maps to /specs.

## 2026-03-23 [Architecture] AGENTS.md is a temporary write target for Codex only — reverted after run: writeCodexAgentsMd() in pipeline.ts appends a fenced direction stack section (between RORCA DIRECTION START/END markers) to AGENTS.md before a Codex run, then removeCodexAgentsMd() restores the original (or deletes the file if Rorca created it) after the run completes. ## 2026-03-23 [Gotcha] Singleton guard blocks worker restart — stale heartbeat survives process kill: When a worker process is killed mid-run (e.g. by SIGKILL), its heartbeat row in worker_heartbeat persists for up to 90 seconds. The singleton guard in the new worker sees the heartbeat and exits with code 0. This cascades via concurrently --kill-others to kill the frontend and server too. Fix: pkill -9 -f "src/worker" to kill ALL worker processes (not just by port), then wait and restart.
> Rule: Singleton guard blocks worker restart — stale heartbeat survives process kill: When a worker process is killed mid-run (e.g. by SIGKILL), its heartbeat row in worker_heartbeat persists for up to 90 seconds. The singleton guard in the new worker sees the heartbeat and exits with code 0. This cascades via concurrently --kill-others to kill the frontend and server too. Fix: pkill -9 -f "src/worker" to kill ALL worker processes (not just by port), then wait and restart.

## 2026-03-23 [Gotcha] concurrently --kill-others kills everything when worker exits with code 0: npm run dev uses concurrently with both --kill-others and --kill-others-on-fail. --kill-others kills ALL processes when ANY process exits, regardless of exit code. So when the worker exits cleanly (code 0) after graceful shutdown, it cascades to kill the frontend and server. This is why restarting the full stack after a worker crash requires killing all three separately.
> Rule: concurrently --kill-others kills everything when worker exits with code 0: npm run dev uses concurrently with both --kill-others and --kill-others-on-fail. --kill-others kills ALL processes when ANY process exits, regardless of exit code. This is why restarting the full stack after a worker crash requires killing all three separately.

## 2026-03-23 [Convention] Three distinct knowledge layers: CLAUDE.md (IS), MEMORY.md (Learned), AGENTS.md (Rules), DB memories (Indexed): CLAUDE.md = declarative handbook of how the system IS built (stack, API routes, gotchas, architecture). MEMORY.md = episodic ledger of what was learned during runs (timestamped, categorized, actionable rules). AGENTS.md = governance of who owns what files and behavioral rules per zone. DB memories table = same content as MEMORY.md but structured, vector-searchable, scored, with embeddings and dedup. Each serves a different injection point and audience.
> Rule: Three distinct knowledge layers: CLAUDE.md (IS), MEMORY.md (Learned), AGENTS.md (Rules), DB memories (Indexed): CLAUDE.md = declarative handbook of how the system IS built (stack, API routes, gotchas, architecture). MEMORY.md = episodic ledger of what was learned during runs (timestamped, categorized, actionable rules). AGENTS.md = governance of who owns what files and behavioral rules per zone. DB memories table = same content as MEMORY.md but structured, vector-searchable, scored, with embeddings and dedup. Each serves a different injection point and audience.

## 2026-03-24 [Gotcha] worker-supervisor.ts stale processes send SIGTERM to new workers — kills the whole dev stack: Stale `worker-supervisor.ts` node processes (started by previous npm run dev sessions) survive after the session ends and send SIGTERM to any new worker that starts, causing cascading --kill-others shutdown of the entire dev stack. Fix: before restarting, run `pkill -9 -f "worker-supervisor" && pkill -9 -f "rorca/backend"` to kill ALL rorca backend processes, not just by port. Port kills alone (lsof -ti:3030) miss the worker and supervisor since they don't bind to a port.
> Rule: worker-supervisor.ts stale processes send SIGTERM to new workers — kills the whole dev stack: Stale `worker-supervisor.ts` node processes (started by previous npm run dev sessions) survive after the session ends and send SIGTERM to any new worker that starts, causing cascading --kill-others shutdown of the entire dev stack. Fix: before restarting, run `pkill -9 -f "worker-supervisor" && pkill -9 -f "rorca/backend"` to kill ALL rorca backend processes, not just by port. Port kills alone (lsof -ti:3030) miss the worker and supervisor since they don't bind to a port.

## 2026-03-24 [Convention] Full clean restart procedure for dev stack: To fully restart the dev stack after crashes or stale process buildup: (1) `pkill -9 -f "rorca/backend"` — kills all tsx server/worker/supervisor processes, (2) `pkill -9 -f "worker-supervisor"` — kills supervisor, (3) `lsof -ti:3030 -ti:5210 | xargs kill -9` — clears ports, (4) wait 3s for heartbeat table to go stale (or wait 90s for full expiry), (5) `npm run dev`. Do NOT rely on port-only kills — the worker and supervisor have no bound port.
> Rule: Full clean restart procedure for dev stack: To fully restart the dev stack after crashes or stale process buildup: (1) `pkill -9 -f "rorca/backend"` — kills all tsx server/worker/supervisor processes, (2) `pkill -9 -f "worker-supervisor"` — kills supervisor, (3) `lsof -ti:3030 -ti:5210 | xargs kill -9` — clears ports, (4) wait 3s for heartbeat table to go stale (or wait 90s for full expiry), (5) `npm run dev`. Do NOT rely on port-only kills — the worker and supervisor have no bound port.

## 2026-03-24 [Bug Fix] Wave-parallel stale skipped flags — stories array and freshSpec were separate refs: In execution-engine.ts, stale flag clearing read a freshSpec from disk and cleared flags on freshSpec.userStories, but the stories array passed to runParallel() was loaded earlier and not updated. Since getStories() returns spec.userStories by reference, clearing must be done directly on the stories array (same object). Fixed by deleting skipped/blocked flags on stories[] directly and writing spec (not freshSpec) back to disk.

## 2026-03-25 [Bug Fix] Express 4 async error handler was broken — routes hung on thrown errors: The Layer.prototype.handle_request patch in async-handler.ts wrapped the original function, but Express 4's original does `try { fn(req, res, next) } catch` WITHOUT returning the Promise. So `result` was always undefined and `.catch(next)` never fired. Any async route that threw (ValidationError, NotFoundError) would hang forever. Fix: replace handle_request entirely, call `this.handle` directly, catch the returned Promise. Affected all routers (memory, agents, etc.) — not just one route.
> Rule: Express 4 async error handler was broken — routes hung on thrown errors: The Layer.prototype.handle_request patch in async-handler.ts wrapped the original function, but Express 4's original does `try { fn(req, res, next) } catch` WITHOUT returning the Promise. So `result` was always undefined and `.catch(next)` never fired. Any async route that threw (ValidationError, NotFoundError) would hang forever. Fix: replace handle_request entirely, call `this.handle` directly, catch the returned Promise. Affected all routers (memory, agents, etc.) — not just one route.

## 2026-03-25 [Architecture] MCP tools auto-inject workspaceId when not provided: In mcp-http.ts, workspaceId is marked optional in Zod schema (so MCP SDK doesn't reject) and executeApiCall() auto-injects the default workspace ID (fetched from GET /api/workspaces?limit=1, cached 1 min). This makes all MCP tools work without users needing to know or specify the workspace ID. The cachedDefaultWorkspaceId + cacheExpiry pattern avoids a DB query on every tool call.
> Rule: MCP tools auto-inject workspaceId when not provided: In mcp-http.ts, workspaceId is marked optional in Zod schema (so MCP SDK doesn't reject) and executeApiCall() auto-injects the default workspace ID (fetched from GET /api/workspaces?limit=1, cached 1 min). This makes all MCP tools work without users needing to know or specify the workspace ID. The cachedDefaultWorkspaceId + cacheExpiry pattern avoids a DB query on every tool call.

## 2026-03-25 [Architecture] MCP /mcp endpoint has scoped CORS separate from /api/* CORS: server.ts has two CORS layers: (1) Global at line ~171 — origin: 'localhost:5210', credentials: true, for browser /api/* routes. (2) MCP-specific mcpCors at line ~218 — origin: true (reflect any), credentials: false, allows Mcp-Session-Id header, scoped to POST/GET/DELETE /mcp only. MCP clients (Claude Code, IDE extensions) connect without browser origin headers so they need the permissive config.

## 2026-03-25 [Bug Fix] Worker crashes on non-fatal AppError unhandledRejections: worker.ts process.on('unhandledRejection') triggered full shutdown on ANY rejection, including ValidationError/NotFoundError from Express routes (statusCode < 500). These are expected business-logic errors, not fatal. Fix: check if reason is an AppError with statusCode < 500 — if so, log warning and return without shutdown. Only truly unexpected rejections trigger shutdown.

## 2026-03-25 [Architecture] rorca_recall_memories now supports 3 retrieval modes: full dump, recent 100, semantic: The MCP `rorca_recall_memories` tool now supports three modes: (1) Full dump (`fetchAll: true`) — returns ALL memories from DB with no limit, (2) Recent (default) — returns last 100 memories ordered by pinned-first then newest (was 20), (3) Semantic (`currentTask` provided) — hits `/api/recall` which triggers the full CAG → RAG → Knowledge Graph cascade and returns top 30 semantically ranked results (was 10). The `currentTask` param is new — it maps to `storyText` on the recall endpoint.

## 2026-03-25 [Gotcha] Dual memory stores (file MEMORY.md vs DB memories table) drift out of sync: Rorca maintains two parallel memory stores: (1) file-based `.rorca/memory/MEMORY.md` read by `memory-ledger.ts`, and (2) PostgreSQL `memories` table. Manual writes and `POST /api/memory` write to both, but synthesis runs and some automated paths only write to the DB. This causes the file to fall behind. The UI MemoryPanel reads from DB (`/api/memory/items`), showing the true count. Any tool reading from the file will see fewer memories. Always prefer DB-backed endpoints for memory retrieval.

## 2026-03-25 [Gotcha] MCP stdio processes must be killed after server.ts code changes — they run old code: When editing `backend/src/mcp/server.ts`, restarting the backend API server (port 3030) is NOT sufficient if Claude Code spawned MCP stdio processes. Those processes (`tsx server.ts` via node) load the old source and keep running until killed. After code changes: `ps aux | grep 'mcp/server.ts' | grep -v grep` to find them, then `kill -9` the PIDs. Claude Code will auto-restart them with the new code.

## 2026-03-25 [Architecture] Memory retrieval cascade: CAG → RAG → Knowledge Graph (memory-router.ts): Semantic memory retrieval uses a 3-tier cascade in `backend/src/lib/memory-router.ts`: (1) CAG — cache-first via `context-cache.ts`, pinned memories always included, (2) RAG — hybrid full-text search via `search.ts` using `tsv @@ plainto_tsquery`, triggered when cache coverage < 50% of key phrases, (3) Graph — Apache AGE knowledge graph via `knowledge-graph.ts` + `graph-context.ts`, traverses file touches and story dependencies. Token budgets: 60% memory, 25% skills, 15% graph (with underflow redistribution). Key phrase extraction uses stopword filtering on words > 4 chars.

Token budgets: 60% memory, 25% skills, 15% graph (with underflow redistribution). Key phrase extraction uses stopword filtering on words > 4 chars.

## 2026-03-30 [Bug Fix] Cross-schema restore: ENUM types missing in public schema block migrations: When restoring a pg_dump from the rorca schema into a fresh instance, migration 061 (spec_attachments) fails with "type attachment_storage_type does not exist". The migration's IF NOT EXISTS check finds the ENUM in the rorca schema (from the dump) and skips CREATE TYPE, but then CREATE TABLE runs with search_path=public and the type isn't there. Fix before first container start: CREATE TYPE public.attachment_storage_type AS ENUM ('database', 's3');
> Rule: Cross-schema restore: ENUM types missing in public schema block migrations: When restoring a pg_dump from the rorca schema into a fresh instance, migration 061 (spec_attachments) fails with "type attachment_storage_type does not exist". The migration's IF NOT EXISTS check finds the ENUM in the rorca schema (from the dump) and skips CREATE TYPE, but then CREATE TABLE runs with search_path=public and the type isn't there. Fix before first container start: CREATE TYPE public.attachment_storage_type AS ENUM ('database', 's3');

## 2026-03-30 [Bug Fix] Cross-schema restore: missing unique constraint on spec_search_index blocks migration 057: After restoring a dump from the rorca schema, migration 057 fails on ON CONFLICT because public.spec_search_index is missing the uq_spec_search_slug_workspace unique constraint (it only exists in rorca schema from the dump). Fix: ALTER TABLE public.spec_search_index ADD CONSTRAINT uq_spec_search_slug_workspace UNIQUE (spec_slug, workspace_id);

## 2026-03-30 [Bug Fix] pg_dump path hardcoded to macOS Homebrew — breaks Docker Alpine runtime: backup.ts had pg_dump binary path hardcoded to /usr/local/opt/postgresql@16/bin/pg_dump (macOS Homebrew). This fails silently in Docker Alpine. Fixed two ways: (1) changed fallback to just 'pg_dump' (uses PATH); (2) added postgresql16-client to the Alpine runtime stage in Dockerfile so pg_dump is available. Set PG_DUMP_BIN env var to override.

## 2026-03-30 [Bug Fix] HSTS + CSP upgrade-insecure-requests break plain-HTTP deployments: Helmet was sending Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=31536000) and upgrade-insecure-requests in CSP unconditionally. On plain HTTP deployments (no TLS), the browser honors HSTS and upgrades all requests to HTTPS → ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR for all assets. Fixed by gating both on HTTPS_ENABLED=1 env var in server.ts. Set HTTPS_ENABLED=1 when serving behind SSL/TLS to re-enable both headers.

Set HTTPS_ENABLED=1 when serving behind SSL/TLS to re-enable both headers.

## 2026-03-30 [Bug Fix] @rollup/rollup-darwin-arm64 in package.json breaks linux/x64 Docker builds: Having @rollup/rollup-darwin-arm64 as a direct dependency in package.json causes EBADPLATFORM errors in Docker linux/x64 builds. It's a Mac M-series specific binary that npm refuses to install on linux/x64. Fix: remove it from package.json dependencies entirely and regenerate package-lock.json. It gets pulled in automatically when needed on Mac.

## 2026-03-30 [Gotcha] HTTPS_ENABLED=1 required to enable HSTS and CSP upgrade-insecure-requests: Helmet sends HSTS and CSP upgrade-insecure-requests conditionally based on HTTPS_ENABLED=1 env var. Without it on a plain HTTP deployment, the browser caches HSTS and forces HTTPS on all subsequent requests causing ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR. Never set HTTPS_ENABLED=1 unless TLS is actually terminated (nginx/Coolify proxy in front).

## 2026-03-30 [Bug Fix] Static files must be served before authRequired middleware: express.static and the SPA catch-all (app.get('*')) must be mounted BEFORE the authRequired middleware block in server.ts. If mounted after, all static assets (JS chunks, CSS, favicon.ico) return 401 Unauthorized to unauthenticated users, breaking the login page entirely. Order: public routes → MCP tools → static files → auth middleware → protected API routes.

## 2026-03-30 [Bug Fix] AuthGate must check isAuthenticated to show login page: The AuthGate component in App.tsx originally had `void isAuthenticated` — deliberately bypassed for local single-user mode. Fixed by adding `if (!isAuthenticated)` check that renders LoginPage/RegisterPage/ForgotPasswordPage. LoginPage and RegisterPage added as module-level lazy imports (not inline inside the function body).

## 2026-03-30 [Bug Fix] GitHub OAuth unconfigured — redirect not JSON: When GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are not set, GET /api/auth/github must redirect to /auth/github/callback?error=github_not_configured (relative URL) rather than returning JSON. Browser navigates directly to this URL so JSON renders raw. Use a relative redirect so it works on any host without hardcoding localhost. The frontend GitHubCallbackPage handles the error param and shows a friendly message.

## 2026-03-30 [Decision] Single-user deployment — registration disabled, GitHub OAuth hidden: VPS deployment is single-user only. POST /api/auth/register returns 403 unless REGISTRATION_DISABLED=false is explicitly set in env. LoginPage no longer shows "Create one" or "Sign in with GitHub" buttons — email/password only. Workspaces have no user_id scoping (all users see all workspaces) so blocking new signups is the only isolation mechanism until proper multi-user workspace scoping is built.

## 2026-03-30 [Gotcha] NetworkBanner hardcoded localhost:3030 caused private network CORS errors: NetworkBanner.tsx had `const HEALTH_URL = 'http://localhost:3030/api/health'` hardcoded. On the VPS, the browser blocked this as a private network access CORS violation (cross-origin from 141.94.33.224:3030 to localhost:3030). Fixed by importing BASE_URL from lib/apiFetch and using `${BASE_URL}/api/health`. BASE_URL is empty string in production builds (relative URL) so health checks go to the same origin.

## 2026-03-30 [Gotcha] Pending migration blocks pipeline trigger — include_graph column: If pipeline trigger hangs indefinitely (curl times out, UI stuck on "Starting..."), check for pending migrations first via GET /api/health — look for `"migrations":{"status":"degraded","pending":N}`. A missing column on pipeline_runs causes the INSERT to fail silently and the backend connection to hang. Fix: apply the migration manually then restart the backend. Root cause: migrations only run on backend startup, so new migrations added while backend is running are never applied until restart.

## 2026-04-03 [Bug Fix] Wave parallel broken by two separate issues: ArchivePanel options drop + waveParallelism config: Wave parallel execution requires two things to be correct simultaneously: (1) ArchivePanel.handleRun must forward all TriggerPopover options (forceSequential, autoMerge, includeGraph) to the pipeline trigger API — since ULT-007, the options parameter was silently dropped, so forceSequential was never sent and backend defaulted to sequential; (2) the target workspace's .rorca/config.json must have waveParallelism: true in the execution block — workspace had it hardcoded to false, blocking wave parallel regardless of UI toggle. Both must be correct or parallelism stays at 1.

Both must be correct or parallelism stays at 1.

## 2026-04-04 [Bug Fix] pg-index.ts isExtensionMigration must include memories and embedding_dimensions: Migration 053_memories.sql uses vector(1536) type which requires pgvector. When pgvector is not installed, it fails non-fatally — but ONLY if the filename matches EXTENSION_MIGRATION_PATTERNS. It doesn't match by default (no 'vector'/'pgvector' in 'memories'). Fix: add 'memories' and 'embedding_dimensions' to EXTENSION_MIGRATION_PATTERNS in pg-index.ts. Same cascading issue: 054/055/059/060/069 all reference the memories table, so they also need the 'memories' pattern. Without this fix, all DB migration tests (QRW-002, QRW-003, etc.) fail in the globalSetup phase.

Same cascading issue: 054/055/059/060/069 all reference the memories table, so they also need the 'memories' pattern. Without this fix, all DB migration tests (QRW-002, QRW-003, etc.) fail in the globalSetup phase.

## 2026-04-06 [Bug Fix] Worker crashes on pg DatabaseError — now non-fatal: The unhandledRejection handler in worker.ts was triggering full shutdown on ANY unhandled rejection, including PostgreSQL errors (missing column, constraint violation). A single bad INSERT (e.g. missing reasoning_tokens column) would close the DB pool and kill the entire server. Fixed by adding isPgError check: if reason instanceof Error and has a string 'code' field (pg error codes like 42703), log and continue — do NOT call shutdown().
> Rule: Worker crashes on pg DatabaseError — now non-fatal: The unhandledRejection handler in worker.ts was triggering full shutdown on ANY unhandled rejection, including PostgreSQL errors (missing column, constraint violation). A single bad INSERT (e.g. missing reasoning_tokens column) would close the DB pool and kill the entire server. Fixed by adding isPgError check: if reason instanceof Error and has a string 'code' field (pg error codes like 42703), log and continue — do NOT call shutdown().

DB is postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca (port 5433). On 2026-04-05: 5 migrations were unapplied (20260403000000 through 20260404000001) causing reasoning_tokens crash.

## 2026-04-06 [Bug Fix] Kill button 409 after backend restart — use direct SIGTERM via PID: After backend restarts, activeProcesses map is wiped. Kill button returns 409 "Process is no longer running" even when the execution engine subprocess is still alive. Workaround: get PID from DB (SELECT pid FROM pipeline_runs WHERE id=...) or ps aux | grep execution-engine, then kill -SIGTERM <pid> directly. The execution engine process survives backend restarts — it is completely independent.

## 2026-04-06 [Gotcha] Server crashes from laptop logout — npm run dev dies on SIGHUP: npm run dev uses concurrently. When macOS sends SIGHUP (screen lock, auto-logout timer), concurrently exits, taking frontend + backend + worker all down. Caffeine prevents display sleep but NOT auto-logout. Check System Settings → Privacy & Security → Advanced → "Log out automatically after X minutes". Permanent fix: run with nohup or launchd plist so server survives logouts. Execution engine subprocesses survive (separate processes) but the worker/backend/frontend die.
> Rule: Server crashes from laptop logout — npm run dev dies on SIGHUP: npm run dev uses concurrently. Check System Settings → Privacy & Security → Advanced → "Log out automatically after X minutes". Permanent fix: run with nohup or launchd plist so server survives logouts. Execution engine subprocesses survive (separate processes) but the worker/backend/frontend die.

Phase 2: add provider prefix if missing. Cascade table in complexity-scorer.ts must use dot format: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6 not anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6.

## 2026-04-06 [Bug Fix] Model escalation/cascade caused surprise OpenRouter charges: The complexity-scorer cascading system in execution-engine.ts silently replaced the user's chosen model (e.g. openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free) with paid models (e.g. openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.6) whenever a story scored as "opus" tier. extractProvider("openrouter/qwen/...") returned "openrouter", cascade table mapped openrouter.opus → "anthropic/claude-opus-4.6", final model became "openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.6" — billed to OpenRouter account. ## 2026-04-06 [Decision] Model resolution: story.model → spec.model → RORCA_MODEL env only: Pipeline execution model resolution chain (as of 2026-04-06): 1) story.model (per-story field in spec JSON userStories), 2) spec.model (top-level spec JSON field, passed as --model CLI flag), 3) RORCA_MODEL env var (system default only). No workspace model, no cascading, no L3 preferred_model direction layer lookup, no workflow_configs.model, no agent_config.agent_model. Never add hidden DB/env fallbacks back into pipeline model resolution — the only valid overrides are spec.model and story.model. If a spec has no model field, the agent runs with RORCA_MODEL env or its own default.

## 2026-04-06 [Bug Fix] OpenCode sub-terminal JSON blobs — MiniTerminalPane had no event filtering: MiniTerminalPane decoded base64 log chunks and passed them raw to the ANSI converter with zero JSON filtering. step_finish events (token counters + git snapshots) and tool_result events (full file contents as escaped JSON) rendered as walls of text. Fixed by adding line-by-line JSON parsing in the chunk handler — suppress step_finish, step_start, tool_result, system, user events before appending to pendingTextRef. The log file still receives all raw bytes (for debugging); only the display path is filtered.
> Rule: OpenCode sub-terminal JSON blobs — MiniTerminalPane had no event filtering: MiniTerminalPane decoded base64 log chunks and passed them raw to the ANSI converter with zero JSON filtering. step_finish events (token counters + git snapshots) and tool_result events (full file contents as escaped JSON) rendered as walls of text. Fixed by adding line-by-line JSON parsing in the chunk handler — suppress step_finish, step_start, tool_result, system, user events before appending to pendingTextRef. The log file still receives all raw bytes (for debugging); only the display path is filtered.

## 2026-04-06 [Bug Fix] OpenCode main terminal JSON blobs — spawnOpenCode dumped all stdout raw: spawnOpenCode in execution-engine.ts did process.stdout.write(chunk) on every byte of OpenCode output without any filtering. step_finish events (contain token counters + git snapshot hashes) and tool_result events (contain full file contents as escaped JSON strings) rendered as giant JSON blobs in the Raw terminal view. Fixed by buffering stdout line-by-line and skipping step_finish, step_start, tool_result event types before forwarding to process.stdout. logStream.write(chunk) still receives everything for the raw log file.

Fixed by buffering stdout line-by-line and skipping step_finish, step_start, tool_result event types before forwarding to process.stdout. logStream.write(chunk) still receives everything for the raw log file.

## 2026-04-06 [Architecture] Two separate terminal data paths — process.stdout vs log file: Main terminal (RunTerminal) reads from run_output_chunks table which is populated from the execution-engine subprocess stdout via the worker. Sub-terminals in wave parallel (MiniTerminalPane) read from per-story log files via /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/stories/:storyId/log SSE endpoint. Any fix to process.stdout filtering does NOT affect sub-terminals. Any fix must be applied independently to both paths.

## 2026-04-06 [Bug Fix] OpenRouter billing leak — anthropic/ prefix caused auto-switch to OpenCode: OPENCODE_PROVIDER_PREFIXES in pipeline.ts included 'anthropic/' which caused Claude models (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6, anthropic/claude-opus-4-6) to auto-switch to OpenCode → OpenRouter, billing API credits instead of using the Claude CLI subscription. Fix: removed 'anthropic/' from the prefix list and added !resolvedAgentModel.startsWith('anthropic/claude-') to the modelIsNonClaude check. When a user selects Claude CLI + Claude model, it stays on Claude CLI (subscription). When they explicitly select OpenCode + any model, it routes through OpenRouter (API key).

## 2026-04-06 [Bug Fix] ModelBadge story override — missing Content-Type header caused 400: apiFetch() does NOT auto-set Content-Type: application/json. Any PUT/POST/PATCH call with JSON.stringify(body) MUST include headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } or Express won't parse the body and required fields like workspaceId will be undefined → 400 error. Also replaced the HTML select element (size attribute listbox) with clickable button list because select onChange doesn't fire when re-selecting the already-selected value.
> Rule: ModelBadge story override — missing Content-Type header caused 400: apiFetch() does NOT auto-set Content-Type: application/json. Any PUT/POST/PATCH call with JSON.stringify(body) MUST include headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } or Express won't parse the body and required fields like workspaceId will be undefined → 400 error. Also replaced the HTML select element (size attribute listbox) with clickable button list because select onChange doesn't fire when re-selecting the already-selected value.

## 2026-04-06 [Bug Fix] Spec JSON agentOverride leaked — rorca-reasoning-engine had agentOverride: opencode with Claude model: Spec JSON files can have agentOverride field set by the SpecModelControlBar. The auto-detection fix in pipeline.ts only prevents auto-switching, NOT explicit overrides. Always check spec JSON for stale agentOverride values before running specs with Claude models.

## 2026-04-06 [Gotcha] Disk full from orphaned worktree node_modules: Worktrees created by wave-parallel runs each get their own node_modules (500MB+ frontend, 275MB+ backend). With 70+ prunable worktrees, this consumed 27GB+. Symptoms: ENOSPC errors, backend crashes, pg-boss can't write jobs. Fix: periodically run 'git worktree prune' and delete node_modules from inactive worktrees. Active worktrees can be identified with 'ps aux | grep execution-engine'.

## 2026-04-06 [Convention] Agent routing rule — Claude models must stay on Claude CLI: When resolving agent type in pipeline.ts: (1) Explicit agentOverride from request or spec JSON takes priority. (2) Auto-detection only switches to OpenCode for non-Claude provider prefixes (openrouter/, openai/, google/, ollama/, github/, bedrock/, vertex/). (3) anthropic/claude-* models must NEVER auto-switch to OpenCode — they use Claude CLI subscription. (4) Bare provider/model strings (e.g. z-ai/glm-5) get openrouter/ prefix added when running on OpenCode.

## 2026-04-06 [Bug Fix] Pending migrations not tracked — manual psql apply skips schema_migrations row: If migrations are applied manually via psql (outside pg-index.ts runner), the schema_migrations tracking row is never inserted. Backend reports status: degraded with N pending migrations. Fix: apply the SQL file via psql, then INSERT INTO rorca.schema_migrations (version, filename) VALUES (...) manually. Always apply migrations through the runner to avoid this.
