## 2026-04-07 [Bug Fix] API server must be restarted for new routes to register — tsx does not hot-reload: The Express API server (src/server.ts) runs under plain `tsx` — NOT `tsx watch`. It does NOT auto-restart on file changes. New routes added to route files (e.g. config.ts) will return 404 until the server process is killed and restarted. Kill with `lsof -ti:3030 | xargs kill -9` then restart. The worker (src/worker.ts) has the same behavior.

Kill with `lsof -ti:3030 | xargs kill -9` then restart. The worker (src/worker.ts) has the same behavior.

## 2026-04-14 [Bug Fix] Specs with all passes=true blocked re-runs — forceRerun feature added: When all stories in a spec had passes=true, the pipeline skipped them all and no new run could be triggered. This was a major blocker — user couldn't re-run completed specs. Fix: added forceRerun param to POST /api/pipeline/trigger (pipeline.ts PipelineTriggerSchema) which resets all passes=true to false in the spec JSON before executing. SpecDetailSlideOver.tsx shows a "Re-run from scratch" button (RotateCcw icon) when allPassed=true. Committed as fc773cc on main.

## 2026-04-14 [Bug Fix] CI TypeScript errors that pass locally but fail in GitHub Actions: Three classes of TS errors slip through local dev but fail CI: (1) unused declared components left in JSX after removing their usage, (2) wrong re-export names in index.ts (e.g. `export type { Bank }` when the actual export is `BankInstitution`), (3) test mock type annotations too narrow (missing optional fields). CI runs `npx tsc --noEmit` from scratch with no incremental cache — local TS Language Server uses cached .tsbuildinfo and misses these. Always run `npx tsc --noEmit` from repo root before pushing.
> Rule: CI TypeScript errors that pass locally but fail in GitHub Actions: Three classes of TS errors slip through local dev but fail CI: (1) unused declared components left in JSX after removing their usage, (2) wrong re-export names in index.ts (e.g. `export type { Bank }` when the actual export is `BankInstitution`), (3) test mock type annotations too narrow (missing optional fields). CI runs `npx tsc --noEmit` from scratch with no incremental cache — local TS Language Server uses cached .tsbuildinfo and misses these. Always run `npx tsc --noEmit` from repo root before pushing.

## 2026-04-14 [Architecture] rorca-ci-autofix spec — 5-story CI feedback loop: New spec `rorca-ci-autofix` (CAF-001–005) approved and ready to run. Implements: (1) CAF-001 — `check_run` webhook handler parsing CI failure annotations into WAL event `ci_check_failed`; (2) CAF-002 — fix-orchestrator subscribes to WAL, generates single-story fix spec, enqueues pipeline run, max 2 attempts per SHA guard; (3) CAF-003 — `ci_autofix_runs` migration table + `ci_autofix_enabled` boolean on workspaces (opt-in, default false) + GET/PATCH `/api/workspaces/:id/ci-autofix` endpoints; (4) CAF-004 — Settings > GitHub tab UI: enable toggle + run history table; (5) CAF-005 — post GitHub commit status back on run completion. Uses `onGithubEvent()` registry + `subscribe()` from sse-hub. Only fires on check runs named `CI Gate*`.
> Rule: rorca-ci-autofix spec — 5-story CI feedback loop: New spec `rorca-ci-autofix` (CAF-001–005) approved and ready to run. Implements: (1) CAF-001 — `check_run` webhook handler parsing CI failure annotations into WAL event `ci_check_failed`; (2) CAF-002 — fix-orchestrator subscribes to WAL, generates single-story fix spec, enqueues pipeline run, max 2 attempts per SHA guard; (3) CAF-003 — `ci_autofix_runs` migration table + `ci_autofix_enabled` boolean on workspaces (opt-in, default false) + GET/PATCH `/api/workspaces/:id/ci-autofix` endpoints; (4) CAF-004 — Settings > GitHub tab UI: enable toggle + run history table; (5) CAF-005 — post GitHub commit status back on run completion. Uses `onGithubEvent()` registry + `subscribe()` from sse-hub. Only fires on check runs named `CI Gate*`.

## 2026-04-14 [Bug Fix] Vite stale module cache causes SyntaxError on case-variant filenames: On macOS (case-insensitive filesystem), Vite can cache a module under two different case variants (e.g. `ArAgingWidget.tsx` vs `ARAgingWidget.tsx`) from a previous HMR cycle. This produces `SyntaxError: Module does not provide export named X` even though the code and imports are correct. Fix: restart the Vite dev server (`lsof -ti:5173 | xargs kill -9 && npm run dev`). No code changes needed.
> Rule: Vite stale module cache causes SyntaxError on case-variant filenames: On macOS (case-insensitive filesystem), Vite can cache a module under two different case variants (e.g. `ArAgingWidget.tsx` vs `ARAgingWidget.tsx`) from a previous HMR cycle. This produces `SyntaxError: Module does not provide export named X` even though the code and imports are correct. Fix: restart the Vite dev server (`lsof -ti:5173 | xargs kill -9 && npm run dev`). No code changes needed.

## 2026-04-14 [Bug Fix] MCP auto-generated tools 30s timeout kills LLM-powered endpoints silently: Auto-generated MCP HTTP tools in `backend/src/lib/mcp-http.ts` have a 30-second default timeout. Only paths in the `SLOW_PATHS` array get 5 minutes. LLM-powered endpoints like `/enrich`, `/match-skills`, `/suggest-skills`, `/add-stories`, `/knowledge-graph` were missing from this list — MCP calls timed out silently while the backend kept processing and completed successfully. The MCP client (Claude Code) reported "Tool timed out" but the operation actually finished with full results (e.g. 21 CAG hits). Fix: add all LLM-powered path fragments to SLOW_PATHS. When adding new LLM-powered API routes, remember to add them to SLOW_PATHS or they'll timeout at 30s via MCP.

LLM-powered endpoints like `/enrich`, `/match-skills`, `/suggest-skills`, `/add-stories`, `/knowledge-graph` were missing from this list — MCP calls timed out silently while the backend kept processing and completed successfully. The MCP client (Claude Code) reported "Tool timed out" but the operation actually finished with full results (e.g. 21 CAG hits). Fix: add all LLM-powered path fragments to SLOW_PATHS. When adding new LLM-powered API routes, remember to add them to SLOW_PATHS or they'll timeout at 30s via MCP.

## 2026-04-14 [Gotcha] Two MCP tool paths for the same API: hand-written (stdio) vs auto-generated (HTTP): Rorca has TWO sets of MCP tools: (1) hand-written tools in `backend/src/mcp/server.ts` (24 tools, stdio transport, use `timedFetch` with 5-min default) and (2) auto-generated tools in `backend/src/lib/mcp-http.ts` (397+ tools from OpenAPI spec, HTTP transport on /mcp, use 30s default timeout). The auto-generated tools are named `rorca_{operation}` (e.g. `rorca_specs_by_id_enrich`) while hand-written ones use shorter names (e.g. `rorca_enrich_spec`). When debugging MCP issues, check WHICH tool was called — they have different timeouts and error handling.
> Rule: Two MCP tool paths for the same API: hand-written (stdio) vs auto-generated (HTTP): Rorca has TWO sets of MCP tools: (1) hand-written tools in `backend/src/mcp/server.ts` (24 tools, stdio transport, use `timedFetch` with 5-min default) and (2) auto-generated tools in `backend/src/lib/mcp-http.ts` (397+ tools from OpenAPI spec, HTTP transport on /mcp, use 30s default timeout). The auto-generated tools are named `rorca_{operation}` (e.g. `rorca_specs_by_id_enrich`) while hand-written ones use shorter names (e.g. `rorca_enrich_spec`). When debugging MCP issues, check WHICH tool was called — they have different timeouts and error handling.

## 2026-04-14 [Bug Fix] spawnClaude: prompt must be piped via stdin, not positional arg: execution-engine.ts spawnClaude() was passing the prompt as a positional CLI argument to `claude --print`. Large prompts (>~32KB, typical for context-routed stories) silently fail — claude exits 0 with zero output and empty log files. Stories appear to "pass" instantly with 0 tokens. Fix: pipe prompt via stdin (stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'], child.stdin.write(prompt), child.stdin.end()). Never pass prompts as positional args to claude CLI.
> Rule: spawnClaude: prompt must be piped via stdin, not positional arg: execution-engine.ts spawnClaude() was passing the prompt as a positional CLI argument to `claude --print`. Large prompts (>~32KB, typical for context-routed stories) silently fail — claude exits 0 with zero output and empty log files. Stories appear to "pass" instantly with 0 tokens. Fix: pipe prompt via stdin (stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'], child.stdin.write(prompt), child.stdin.end()). Never pass prompts as positional args to claude CLI.

## 2026-04-14 [Bug Fix] spawnClaude --mcp-config: HTTP URLs cause silent exit 0: Claude CLI --mcp-config only supports stdio command/args format ({"command":"node","args":[...]}). Passing HTTP URLs ({"type":"http","url":"http://localhost:4041/mcp"}) causes claude to silently exit 0 with zero output. Fix: write stdio command/args format for known MCP servers (chrome-devtools, playwright). OpenCode uses {"type":"remote","url":...} in opencode.json (native HTTP support). Codex uses `codex mcp add --url` (native HTTP support). Only Claude CLI has this limitation.
> Rule: spawnClaude --mcp-config: HTTP URLs cause silent exit 0: Claude CLI --mcp-config only supports stdio command/args format ({"command":"node","args":[...]}). Passing HTTP URLs ({"type":"http","url":"http://localhost:4041/mcp"}) causes claude to silently exit 0 with zero output. Fix: write stdio command/args format for known MCP servers (chrome-devtools, playwright). OpenCode uses {"type":"remote","url":...} in opencode.json (native HTTP support). Codex uses `codex mcp add --url` (native HTTP support). Only Claude CLI has this limitation.

## 2026-04-14 [Bug Fix] MCP server health-check: ensure functions must verify liveness every call: ensureChromeDevToolsMcpServer() and ensurePlaywrightMcpServer() cached _chromeMcpReady/_playwrightMcpReady as true after first successful start, but never re-verified. If the MCP server process died between stories, subsequent stories got a stale URL pointing to a dead server. Fix: on every call when _ready=true, probe the HTTP endpoint. If probe fails, reset state and restart the server.
> Rule: MCP server health-check: ensure functions must verify liveness every call: ensureChromeDevToolsMcpServer() and ensurePlaywrightMcpServer() cached _chromeMcpReady/_playwrightMcpReady as true after first successful start, but never re-verified. If the MCP server process died between stories, subsequent stories got a stale URL pointing to a dead server. Fix: on every call when _ready=true, probe the HTTP endpoint. If probe fails, reset state and restart the server.

Journey mode specs browse the live app via Chrome DevTools MCP — they exit 0 with no file modifications by design. The gate must check `mode === 'journey'` and skip entirely.

## 2026-04-15 [Architecture] node-pty graceful degradation — try/catch at module load, not import time: When integrating native N-API modules like node-pty, wrap require() in a try/catch at module load (not dynamic import()). Set a module-scoped PTY_AVAILABLE boolean. Check this flag before calling native module functions and throw structured errors ({ code, message }) that routes can catch and convert to 503 Service Unavailable. This allows the server to start successfully even when the native module is not built, with the feature gracefully disabled.
> Rule: node-pty graceful degradation — try/catch at module load, not import time: When integrating native N-API modules like node-pty, wrap require() in a try/catch at module load (not dynamic import()). Set a module-scoped PTY_AVAILABLE boolean. Check this flag before calling native module functions and throw structured errors ({ code, message }) that routes can catch and convert to 503 Service Unavailable. This allows the server to start successfully even when the native module is not built, with the feature gracefully disabled.

## 2026-04-16 [Bug Fix] Terminal WebSocket output dropped — session.outputSequence vs nextSequence: server.ts used `session.outputSequence` but PtySession interface defines `nextSequence`. undefined += 1 → NaN → JSON null → frontend sequence check (null <= 0 === true) silently dropped every WebSocket output message. Keystrokes were sent to PTY but echoes never reached xterm. Fix: use session.nextSequence in server.ts WebSocket onData handler.
> Rule: Terminal WebSocket output dropped — session.outputSequence vs nextSequence: server.ts used `session.outputSequence` but PtySession interface defines `nextSequence`. undefined += 1 → NaN → JSON null → frontend sequence check (null <= 0 === true) silently dropped every WebSocket output message. Keystrokes were sent to PTY but echoes never reached xterm. Fix: use session.nextSequence in server.ts WebSocket onData handler.

File: backend/src/routes/terminal.ts validateWsToken().

React StrictMode double-mounts effects: first mount consumes token, cleanup closes connection, second mount rejected. Fix: keep token in map until TTL expiry (60s) instead of deleting on first use. File: backend/src/routes/terminal.ts validateWsToken().

Also: TerminalPanel callback props (onExit, onInput, onTitleChange, onBell) were inline arrows — captured via refs instead.

## 2026-04-16 [Bug Fix] qa-accrual-missing-flows worktree spec was stale (10 stories vs 17 in main): The worktree at workspace-feat-qa-accrual-missing-flows had an old 10-story spec (AMF-001–010, all passes=False). ## 2026-04-16 [Gotcha] Multiple stale server/worker processes cause silent job failures: When npm run dev is started multiple times (e.g. once manually, once via mprocs), you get duplicate server and worker processes on the same ports. The stale worker (old PID, old code) can claim pg-boss jobs before the fresh worker does. Runs appear to start (status=running) but the engine never spawns (pid=NULL, last_heartbeat=NULL) and state reconciliation marks them failed in ~30s. Always kill ALL node processes before starting: `lsof -ti:3030 | xargs kill -9; lsof -ti:5210 | xargs kill -9; ps aux | grep -E "(server|worker)\.ts" | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2}' | xargs kill -9`
> Rule: Multiple stale server/worker processes cause silent job failures: When npm run dev is started multiple times (e.g. once manually, once via mprocs), you get duplicate server and worker processes on the same ports. The stale worker (old PID, old code) can claim pg-boss jobs before the fresh worker does. Runs appear to start (status=running) but the engine never spawns (pid=NULL, last_heartbeat=NULL) and state reconciliation marks them failed in ~30s. Always kill ALL node processes before starting: `lsof -ti:3030 | xargs kill -9; lsof -ti:5210 | xargs kill -9; ps aux | grep -E "(server|worker)\.ts" | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2}' | xargs kill -9`

## 2026-04-16 [Decision] StoryCard Linear-style status treatment — dot icon + dimming, no colored ID or DONE badge: Story cards now follow Linear's UX pattern: (1) story ID is always muted gray — never colored by status; (2) status dot left of title: Circle=not done, CheckCircle2=done (muted), MinusCircle=deferred; (3) done rows dim to opacity-50 + border-border/50 + title goes text-muted; (4) DONE text badge removed entirely. Done stories recede visually, unfinished stories demand attention.
> Rule: StoryCard Linear-style status treatment — dot icon + dimming, no colored ID or DONE badge: Story cards now follow Linear's UX pattern: (1) story ID is always muted gray — never colored by status; (2) status dot left of title: Circle=not done, CheckCircle2=done (muted), MinusCircle=deferred; (3) done rows dim to opacity-50 + border-border/50 + title goes text-muted; (4) DONE text badge removed entirely. Done stories recede visually, unfinished stories demand attention.

## 2026-04-16 [Bug Fix] Vite worktree process persists on port 5173 after killing main processes: When a spec run creates a worktree (e.g. workspace-feat-qa-accrual-missing-flows), that worktree's Vite dev server may still be running independently. Killing the main workspace processes does not kill the worktree's Vite. Result: new mprocs Vite bumps to 5174, old browser tab on 5173 still works. Find with: `lsof -ti:5173 | xargs ps -p` then kill the worktree Vite PID separately.
> Rule: Vite worktree process persists on port 5173 after killing main processes: When a spec run creates a worktree (e.g. workspace-feat-qa-accrual-missing-flows), that worktree's Vite dev server may still be running independently. ## 2026-04-21 [Architecture] Merge Strategy — 4-way post-run routing: Worktree runs support 4 merge strategies: direct (merge+push main), pr (push branch+create PR), draft-pr (push branch+create draft PR), branch-only (push branch, no PR/merge). Resolved from: per-run trigger override > spec JSON mergeStrategy field > workspace pipeline_config.mergeStrategy > 'direct' fallback. Implemented in worker.ts switch statement, pg-boss-schemas.ts MergeStrategyEnum, pipeline.ts trigger route, and TriggerPopover.tsx dropdown UI.

Resolved from: per-run trigger override > spec JSON mergeStrategy field > workspace pipeline_config.mergeStrategy > 'direct' fallback. Implemented in worker.ts switch statement, pg-boss-schemas.ts MergeStrategyEnum, pipeline.ts trigger route, and TriggerPopover.tsx dropdown UI.

## 2026-04-21 [Bug Fix] Worker spec completion check gated behind exit code: The worker's post-run merge/PR logic was gated on status === 'done', meaning if the engine exited non-zero (timeout, signal, crash) but all stories actually passed in the spec JSON, the merge strategy never fired. Fixed by reading spec JSON regardless of exit code. If allSpecStoriesPassed is true but status is 'failed', the run is promoted to 'done' in the DB and merge strategy proceeds. Ground truth is the spec file, not the exit code.
> Rule: Worker spec completion check gated behind exit code: The worker's post-run merge/PR logic was gated on status === 'done', meaning if the engine exited non-zero (timeout, signal, crash) but all stories actually passed in the spec JSON, the merge strategy never fired. Fixed by reading spec JSON regardless of exit code. If allSpecStoriesPassed is true but status is 'failed', the run is promoted to 'done' in the DB and merge strategy proceeds. Ground truth is the spec file, not the exit code.

## 2026-04-21 [Architecture] LLM-synthesized diff summary in auto-PR bodies: github-pr-creator.ts now runs git diff main...branch through chatComplete to generate a truthful bullet-point summary of what was actually built (not what the spec planned). The synthesized summary replaces spec.brief as the primary PR summary. Spec brief is shown as a blockquote for context. Diff is truncated to 50k chars for LLM context limits. Falls back to spec brief if synthesis fails. Template variable is {{run.diffSummary}}.

Falls back to spec brief if synthesis fails. Template variable is {{run.diffSummary}}.

## 2026-04-21 [Decision] Merge strategy is spec-level declarative, not path-based: The merge strategy is a declarative property on the spec JSON (mergeStrategy field), workspace config, or per-run override. It is NOT based on analyzing file paths, migration detection, or risk scoring. Rorca remains a generic agnostic orchestration platform — it doesn't know or care what a "migration" is. The user or spec author declares the intent explicitly.
